'''Klaus Kilimann''' (11 October 1938 – 26 May 2024) was a German physicist who became an SPD politician after [[Die Wende|1989]]. Between 1990 and 1993 he served as [[Lord Mayor|Oberbürgermeister]] of [[Rostock]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenKK>{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=1695|author1= [[Helmut Müller-Enbergs]] |title =Kilimann, Klaus * 11.10.1938 Oberbürgermeister von Rostock|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |accessdate= 30 January 2015}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Kilimann was born in East Prussia. His father was a [[Deutsche Reichsbahn|railway]] worker. He began attending primary school in [[Szczytno|Ortelsburg]], his birthplace, which was at the time in Germany. By the time the [[Red army]] arrived in January 1945 most of the population had fled, however, and in 1944 or 1945 Kilimann was among the millions of Germans [[Flight and expulsion of Germans from Poland during and after World War II|forcibly relocated]] in a westward direction. The family ended up in [[Neukloster]] not far from [[Rostock]] in the [[Soviet occupation zone]] of what remained of Germany, and it was here that he concluded his primary education and then attended a [[Extended Secondary School (East Germany)|secondary school]] till 1956.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenKK/>

From 1956 Kilimann attended the [[University of Rostock]] from where he emerged in 1961 with a degree in [[Physics]]. He then undertook post-graduate studies at [[Moscow State University]] till 1963, when he returned to Rostock and took a university post as a research assistant at the [[Mathematics]] department. He transferred to the [[Physics]] department in 1964 which was also the year in which he received his doctorate. He remained at the university as a senior research assistant from 1970 till 1979, having in 1978 produced his [[:de:Habilitationsschrift|Habilitation dissertation]] on a topic in [[theoretical physics]].<ref>His habilitation dissertation was entitled ''"Zwei-Teilchen-Zustände in Fermisystemen mit Coulombwechselwirkung"''. <br> Any reader who understands enough about theoretical physics (and can follow the German) is invited to insert a translation.</ref> Between 1980 and 1990 he was employed as an associate professor.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenKK/> During that period, however, for three years from 1982 he was based in [[Nicaragua]], helping to set up a Physics education department at an academy in the capital, [[Managua]].<ref>Klaus Kilimann: ''Deutsch-Deutsche Beziehungen im Sandinistischen Nicaragua'', in: Erika Harzer, Willi Volks (Hrsg.): ''Aufbruch nach Nicaragua'', Ch. Links, Berlin, 2009, {{ISBN|978-3-86153-525-6}}</ref>

In October 1989 Kilimann became a member of [[New Forum]] in Rostock. New Forum was a quasi-political party, sometimes described as a "citizens' initiative", that emerged during the second half of 1989 in the context of growing civil unrest in the country. As a member, Kilimann participated locally in the legal committee set up within the wider context of the [[:de:Runder Tisch|Round Table]] discussions that were established in various parts of the country as part of what was now becoming known as East Germany's [[Die Wende|Peaceful Revolution]]. In January 1990, having quit New Forum, Kilimann joined the newly (in East Germany) re-formed [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR|Social Democratic Party (SDP)]] which had till October 1989 been [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|effectively muted]] following the creation in 1946 of the East German [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Socialist Unity Party]]. In October 1990, with the formal [[German reunification|reunification]] of East and West Germany, the East German SDP and (hitherto West German) SPD merged, which made Kilimann a member of the German [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party (SPD)]].

On 31 May 1990, Kilimann was elected [[Lord Mayor]] of Rostock in succession to [[:de:Christoph Kleemann|Christoph Kleemann]]. He resigned the office three and a half years later on 3 December 1993,<ref name=NYTKKRueckt>{{cite web |periodical=The New York Times|title=German Official Quits Over Riots|date=13 November 1993|access-date=31 January 2015|author=[[Stephen Kinzer]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/11/13/world/german-official-quits-over-riots.html}}</ref> following reports on race riots targeting asylum-seekers, fourteen months earlier, in August 1992.<ref name=NYTKKRueckt/> The reports concluded that local police chiefs and political leaders had permitted tensions to fester and then failed act quickly and decisively when rioting broke out.<ref name=NYTKKRueckt/> Kilimann himself had been out of town when the riots started and returned from his break only as the violence reached its third night.<ref name=NYTKKRueckt/> After his resignation Kilimann was unemployed for a period till September 1994.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenKK/>

From 1994 till his retirement in 2005 Kilimann worked on a succession of consultancy projects on behalf of the [[Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development|German Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development]]. The consultancy work took him to [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Moscow]] and [[Kyrgyzstan]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenKK/>

Kilimann died on 26 May 2024, at the age of 85.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manfred-Klaus Kilimann |url=https://trauer-anzeigen.de/traueranzeige/manfred-klaus-kilimann |website=trauer-anzeigen.de |access-date=2 June 2024}}</ref>
